chapter_theme: Natrinai 341 to 360: a war-camp soldier and a road-weary traveller who picture the women they left, wives who refuse the husband back from courtesans, friends who use proverb, gossip and the mother's misreading to push the man to marry, a woman who prays to the oath-god for the lover who broke his word, and a sleepless woman who asks whether the whole rejoicing world is fighting her; with Kolli of Porayan, Iruppai of Viraan and Marungai of Valuthi as measures of beauty.

341.reading: Alone in the war camp on a hostile frontier, where cool rain has poured, water drips through half the night and the north wind of a strange land buffets him in the cold season, the man pictures the girl at home well companioned: tired of the vangaa bird's small song she plays with a red-spotted lac piece, drinks her milk without losing her laughter, waves a harmless twig and trades little riddles with the hill man and her kin, while he is without companion, alone, in the camp.
341.nuance: The poem turns on the double துணை: she has companions in plenty (துணை நன்கு உடையள்), he has none (துணை இலேம்). Rather than imagine her pining, he envies her company, which makes his own loneliness the subject. Lines 1 to 4 describe her games in rare words (வட்டு நா வடிக்கும், அலையா உலவை), and their exact sense is not sure.

colophon.thurai: வினைவயிற் பிரிந்து ஆற்றானாகிய தலைமகன் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the cold season, the middle of the night and the hill home fix kurinji's time and land

comparisons.tenor: the man alone in camp (துணை இலேம், line 10), set against the girl among her companions

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; he speaks to himself in the camp

342.reading: The friend, who agreed to carry the man's plea, says to herself that she took his words into her mouth as one takes a palmyra stem for a horse and rides the madal, or a mirage for a wall and climbs it: she told the girl that one who has love must always be gracious to those who come to her from another street, put it sweetly, and still the girl would not take it; now she even thinks of laying at the girl's red feet his head, striped with the bee-sipped flowers of the shore grove, and wonders what would come of that.
342.nuance: The madal, the man's last threat, is here the friend's own image for her errand: she has ridden a palm stem as if it were a horse. Taking the mirage (வெண் தேர்) for a wall is a second figure of the same self-deception. The last lines may mean she will bring him to fall at the girl's feet; the syntax of lines 7 to 10 is compressed.

colophon.thurai: குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம்புக்க தன் சொல் கேளாது விடலின் இறப்ப ஆற்றான் ஆயினான் என உணர்ந்து ஆற்றாளாய்த் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது தலைமகனுக்குக் குறை நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம் புக்கலளாய் ஆற்றாது தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove is the only land named

comparisons.vehicle: மா என மதித்து மடல் ஊர்ந்து ஆங்கு மதில் என மதித்து வெண் தேர் ஏறி
comparisons.tenor: the friend's carrying of a plea that cannot succeed

343.reading: The woman asks her friend whether there is no such evening in the land where her lover went, leaving them to seek hard-won wealth: here, in the small village off the stony mullai-covered path, where cows rub their backs on the long-rooted banyan of the god in the dung-dusted street, the crow that ate the spilt offerings goes to crowd in with its kin in the sad dusk, and the grieving evening comes as if with an army.
343.nuance: The question is whether evening exists where he is: if it did, he could not stay. The colophon files it under paalai for the parting, but nothing in the poem is of the road; the village, cows, mullai and evening are all mullai.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகள் பிரிவிடை ஆற்றாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the woman bearing the evening at home while he is away is mullai's waiting

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the poem says வாழி தோழி

iraicchi.act: the crow, fed on the offerings, goes at dusk to crowd in with its own kin
iraicchi.sense: even the crow goes home to its own at evening, while the man stays away in the far land for wealth

344.reading: With the man listening unseen, the friend tells the girl that if they are set to guard the great field of dark millet on the hill slope, its heads bent like a she-elephant's trunk, he will not learn how things stand with them; will he simply go home, bees humming along the long slope at his sandal-smeared chest, to his town of rich rocks, where people mistake the roar of a tiger that has killed an elephant in the echoing cave for thunder and gather up the red millet drying in the yard?
344.nuance: Meant for the man's ears: once the millet is ripe the field-watch, and with it their meetings, will end. The closing scene, where a tiger's roar is taken for thunder and the drying millet is hurried in, is a near miss for ullurai (an alarm misread and a harvest gathered in might answer to gossip and the girl kept indoors), but neither pair is anchored in the poem, so it is scene.

colophon.thurai: தோழி சிறைப்புறமாகத் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: millet fields, the tiger and the elephant are kurinji things

comparisons.tenor: the heavy bent heads of the millet

345.reading: To the lord of the shore, where the green fruit of the kandal drops into the dark blue backwater and the water lily, swung by the strong wind, opens white like a small white gull yawning, the friend says: if even upright men like you, who have taken on nobility and whose friendship is always kind and great, delay and do not want her, so that her unassured heart withers helplessly, what is the use of living; let assurance perish.
345.nuance: The curse falls on தெளிவு itself, the assurance he gave: if even the noble do not keep it, let trust perish. The falling fruit that sets the lily swinging open is a near miss for ullurai, with only one pair (his act, her opening), so it is scene.

colophon.thurai: தௌ¢விடை விலங்கியது

thinai_evidence.note: mangrove, backwater and the shore lord fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names neither speaker nor addressee; the poem addresses the shore lord (துறைவ), and the speaker pleads for another's heart, so the friend is assumed

346.reading: The man, on the hard frontier road where kings speak of war, in a small village with its fence destroyed and its common empty and swept by lingering wind, in the season when cool rain clouds drawn from the eastern sea have darkened the west and cooled the land, tells his heart that it seemed to laugh today at the thought of the broad soft shoulders of his young wife, whose hair smells of the small green kulavi of the great cool Kolli of Porayan, who shines like the full moon.
346.nuance: The rains of line 2 are mullai's season and the kulavi of Kolli a kurinji flower, so the road poem is mixed. Lines 6 and 7 (தாள் வலி ஆகிய வன்கண் இருக்கை / இன்று நக்கனைமன் போலா) are hard: the heart may have laughed once, or seem to laugh now, at the memory.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகன் ஆற்றானாய்த் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the man away on a hard, war-torn road, his heart turning home, is paalai's parting

347.reading: The woman tells her friend that the bards who praise in many ways the lord of the great hill, where in the rain the great cloud, heavy with the roaring sea, hides the directions, shakes the high peaks, strikes the snakes and pours, and the falls come down sounding like a drum struck on its left face by the drummer, calling him as steady as water and full of love, make grand speeches as pitiable as frogs in summer; will her beauty come back for the sight of such praise?
347.nuance: The praise she scorns is the bards' (பரிசிலர்), the professional voices of puram; she turns their நெடுமொழி, the word for a hero's vaunt, into the croaking of frogs in a season with no rain, so the court's praise is weighed against a man who will not marry.

colophon.thurai: வரையாது நெடுங்காலம் வந்தொழுக ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுக்க மறுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the falls of the great hill fix kurinji

comparisons.vehicle: புலையன் பேழ் வாய்த் தண்ணுமை இடம் தொட்டன்ன

comparisons.tenor: the man's steady nature as the bards praise it

348.reading: The woman says the moon has spread its many rays across the blue sky like a sea full of milk, the town in its noisy crowds celebrates a festival in its busy streets, in every flower-thick grove the bees hum with the mates they love, and she alone, her jewels slipping, in lonely grief, has no sleep through the dense dark night; so is this world fighting her, or is her grieving heart fighting the world?
348.nuance: Three ‑ஏ clauses (நிலவே, ஊரே, கானே) set out the full world before the fourth, யானே, sets her apart; the closing question will not settle whether she or the world is at fault.

colophon.thurai: வேட்கை பெருகத் தாங்கலளாய் ஆற்றாமை மீதூர்கின்றாள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: lonely grief and sleeplessness are neythal's lament; the poem names no land

comparisons.tenor: the moonlight spread over the sky

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the last line speaks to her heart (நெஞ்சே)

iraicchi.act: the bees hum through the groves together with the mates they love
iraicchi.sense: even the bees have their partners beside them tonight, while she lies alone without hers

349.reading: The man says to himself, the friend listening, that riding his swift chariot or going on foot, plucking adumbu flowers by the curving backwater, lifting the screw-pine and picking the neythal, his heart feeling as if they had already met, he is distressed day after day; and he asks what the fisher girl can think of him, who never tires of hanging back behind her like the ghoul that hovers by men gravely wounded in the camp's spear-bright battlefield, where crowned kings fell and elephants were killed.
349.nuance: He gathers her shore's flowers as if gathering her, then sees himself as she must: a battlefield ghoul waiting by the wounded. The simile brings a whole puram scene into a love poem.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் தோழி கேட்பத் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: shore flowers and the fisher folk fix neythal

comparisons.tenor: the man who keeps following behind the girl

350.reading: The wife tells the man that even if her old beauty, like Iruppai of Viraan of the generous chariots, where the reapers' drum in the white paddy scares the many birds of the field into flight and the hanging clusters of the bent marutham drop, should perish, let it; she will not let him near, for to embrace him, his sandal crushed by the round breasts of another and his garland withered, would be like clasping a vessel that gives no hold; do not come, and long life to the woman who held you.
350.nuance: She stakes her beauty, which is a prosperous town, on the refusal: let it wane rather than let him in. The crushed sandal and withered garland are the evidence she reads off his body. ஆசு இல் கலம் is obscure: a vessel without a grip, or without a flaw, which would reverse the sense.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகள் ஊடல் மறுத்தாள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: paddy reapers, field birds and the marutham tree fix the watered land

comparisons.tenor: embracing the man fresh from the other woman

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: ஊடல் மறுத்தாள் is read as her refusing to end the sulk

351.reading: The friend tells the mother that, saying the girl had outgrown childhood, she shut her in strict guard in the rich house, yet does not see that the girl has only grown paler; let her not toil for many days worshipping the gods with a troubled heart: if the girl guarded the wide field of small millet from the platform of tiger hide, fearless of the elephant's might, built of sandalwood in the fork of the black-trunked vengai, she would surely get her beauty back.
351.nuance: The cure she prescribes is the cause: the millet field is where the girl meets the man. Her words tell the mother as much as can be told without confessing the affair.

colophon.thurai: தோழி அருகு அடுத்தது

thinai_evidence.note: the vengai, the watch platform and the millet field fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the addressee is the mother (அன்னை, line 5)

352.reading: Halfway through the waste, the man says to himself that on this fearful forked road, where loveless men with bows and leaf-bladed arrows have killed many travellers, the old fat-loving jackal, driving off the cock bird with fire-red ears, runs with its shadow, gorges on raw flesh, grows hot, searches the bare mirage-bright ground for water and finds no shelter even in the shade of the cairns; the road has been hard even for him, so how has she come, the fine young girl of bamboo shoulders, pitiable as she is?
352.nuance: The closing question may mean she has come to him in thought across a road too hard for him, which is the likeliest reading, or that she followed him; the poem does not settle it.

colophon.thurai: பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகன் இடைச் சுரத்துக்கண் ஆற்றானாய்த் தன்னுள்ளே சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hard waste and the bare ground fix paalai

comparisons.tenor: the red ears of the cock bird

353.reading: The friend tells the lord of the sky-touching hill, where clouds drift in flocks over the high peaks like the fine thread that husbandless women spin by hand, and the hill people's dear young daughter feasts the black-fingered female monkey on the pot-sized fruit of an old bent jackfruit tree as on an arriving guest, that he is not noble, even if their love ripens, because he comes at midnight on the fearful narrow path where the great elephant that killed a tiger roars like fierce thunder.
353.nuance: சான்றோய் அல்லை is a hard word for a lover: his nobility is measured by whether he spares her the fear of his night journey.

colophon.thurai: தோழி ஆற்றது அருமை அஞ்சி தான் ஆற்றாளாய்ச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: jackfruit, hill people and the monkey fix kurinji

comparisons.vehicle: ஆள் இல் பெண்டிர் தாளின் செய்த நுணங்கு நுண் பனுவல் போல

iraicchi.act: the hill girl feeds the jackfruit to the monkey, treating it as an arriving guest
iraicchi.sense: in this country a guest who comes openly is fed and made welcome, so the man should come as a guest by marriage, not by the fearful night path

354.reading: The friend asks the man how the girl is to bear it, and tells him that at the spray-wet shore of the grove, with its yard of long sand near the grove fenced with fallen fronds of the tall dark palmyra and a small boat tied to the trunk of the punnai dark as night, his friendship has become gossip as loud as the din of the salt men watching their carts of sun-boiled salt move in rows down the long road.
354.nuance: The long description is of the girl's own yard, now a place he cannot reach; the salt carts are the noise of trade, and his secret love has become as public as a market.

colophon.thurai: தோழியால் செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇ வரைவு கடாயது மனைவயின் தோழியைத் தலைமகன் புகழ்ந்தாற்கு மறுத்துச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: palmyra, punnai and the salt pans fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: on this reading the man praises the friend at the house (மனைவயின்) and she turns the praise aside

355.reading: The friend tells the lord of the land, where the kaandal cluster touches the plump banana leaf as a flower-eyed young mother who has borne a son presses her breast to his mouth, and the red-faced monkey drinks the sweet falls-water caught on the leaf, that the truly refined will drink even poison if friends of long standing offer it; even if he finds no joy at heart in sleeping on her friend's shoulders, let him be kind for her sake, for the girl has nothing but him.
355.nuance: She asks him to act by கண் ஓடி, kindly regard, with the proverb of the poison as her proof: a refined man takes even what he does not want from a friend. The kaandal that guides the falls-water to the monkey like a mother's hand is a near miss for ullurai (the hand that offers maps to the friend who offers the girl, but no second pair holds), so it is a simile and scene.

colophon.thurai: தோழி அருகு அடுத்தது தோழி தலைமகளது ஆற்றாமை கண்டு வரைவு கடாயதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: kaandal, the falls and the monkey fix kurinji

comparisons.vehicle: புதல்வன் ஈன்ற பூங் கண் மடந்தை முலை வாய் உறுக்கும் கை போல்
comparisons.tenor: the kaandal cluster pressing on the banana leaf

356.reading: Refused the girl in marriage, the man tells his heart that it has toiled going and coming like the tireless strong wings of the red-legged swan with soft crossing feathers, which grazes in the clear sea where the land lies low and carries the gathered food to its unfledged chicks on the peak of the tall gold-bearing Himalaya, haunt of the celestial women; one day, with his beloved beside him, joy will come to them too, like the morning star rising in the east.
356.nuance: The swan's flight spans the whole land, from the southern sea to the Himalaya, and it flies to feed young that cannot yet fly: the heart's errands are for a future household. The morning star is an omen of the good day.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு மறுக்கப்பட்டு ஆற்றானாகிய தலைமகன் தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the hope of union after a refused proposal is kurinji's; the swan of the sea comes in only as a simile

comparisons.tenor: the day of union to come

357.reading: The woman asks her friend what she means to do, and says that her own mind, though it does not stay with her, never fades but has scarred her heart: the day she played with the man of the slopes, wearing a garland of blue lilies like her kohl eyes, gathered from the wide green pool among the rocks of the grove on the far-seen hillside where the peacock with gem-spotted crest dances after drying from the rain, the garland loosened by the tossing water.
357.nuance: The peacock that dances once it has dried after the rain is close to her own case, but it only shows a mood and does nothing a person of the situation does, so it is scene. The poet is a woman, Kurumakal Kuriyeyini.

colophon.thurai: தலைமகன் வரைவு நீடிய இடத்து ஆற்றுவல் என்பது படச் சொல்லியது மனை மருண்டு வேறுபாடாயினாய் என்ற தோழிக்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: peacock, hill pool and the man of the slopes fix kurinji

comparisons.tenor: the blue lilies of her garland

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon's first reading names no speaker; the poem's தோழி and the memory make it the woman

358.reading: The woman tells her friend: since he, ashamed to see her so, her broad shoulders slack, her fine lines fading and pallor spreading over her small soft chest, swore assurances to the friend, let them go scatter high offerings to the god who dwells with its host and pray, long life to you, never harm him in any way, though he is the one hard enough to stay away there while her rare beauty, like Marungai of Valuthi of the green jewels, where the small white gull gets its daily food of the curled-headed big red shrimp, fades.
358.nuance: The god punishes broken oaths, so the woman, the one wronged, prays for the oath-breaker's safety. The prayer reassures the friend while it names his fault.

colophon.thurai: பட்டபின்றை வரையாது பொருள்வயிற் பிரிந்த காலத்து தோழி இவள் ஆற்றா ளாயினாள் இவளை இழந்தேன் எனக் கவன்றாள் வற்புறுத்தது அக்காலத்து ஆற்றாளாய் நின்ற தலைமகள் தோழிக்குச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the shrimp and the white gull of the shore fix neythal

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the woman reassures the friend who feared she would not survive

359.reading: The friend says the lord of the hill land, where a small-horned red cow grazing the slope brushes the swaying kaandal and is so covered in pollen that her calf does not know her, has given them a leaf skirt to wear; if they wear it they fear the mother, if they give it back they fear hurting the kinsman; meanwhile will those leaves wither, so hard to pluck from his hill's god-haunted slopes where even the fighting mountain goats do not leap?
359.nuance: The gift is precious because of where it grew: leaves from slopes even the goats will not climb. The friend's dilemma, between the mother and the man, is set out in two balanced clauses (உடுப்பின் ... கொடுப்பின்).

colophon.thurai: தோழி தழையேற்றுக் கொண்டு நின்று தலைமகன் குறிப்பின் ஓடியது

thinai_evidence.note: kaandal, the slope and the mountain goat fix kurinji

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the poem's யாம் speaks for both women, so the girl is assumed

ullurai.tenor: the girl marked by the man's gift, and her mother

pairs.situation: the girl who wears the leaves from his hill is marked by them
the mother would find her daughter changed and grow alarmed

ullurai.speaker_fit: the friend uses a cow, its calf and the kaandal of the hill slope in a kurinji poem (porul 7.27)

360.reading: The friend tells the man to go and win the soft shoulders of the women brought today, having taken the fresh beauty of those he joined yesterday and left them like the doll in the festival ground after the festival, when the drums' faces have dried and the turns of dancing are done; may his courtesans flourish; she is glad at the great distress he has come to, which he wastes like the morsel that an elephant in a sulk, goaded with spikes by its keepers, smears over its body instead of eating; and the lazy sleep of the house will come again.
360.nuance: The festival doll is the courtesans' fate, not the wife's: he uses each woman for a day. Lines 6 to 11 are hard; whose shame (பல்லோர் பழித்தல் நாணி) and whose sleep is meant is not certain.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையிற் பிரிந்த தலைமகனைத் தோழி தலைமகள் குறிப்பறிந்து வாயில் மறுத்தது தலைமகள் ஊடிச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man's going to courtesans and the refusal at the door are marutham's oodal

comparisons.vehicle: முழவு முகம் புலர்ந்து முறையின் ஆடிய விழவு ஒழி களத்த பாவை போல
comparisons.tenor: the women he enjoyed yesterday and abandoned
the man's distress, got and wasted

links.note: Both are cold-season war-camp poems that end on the same turn, யாமே ... பாசறையேமே: in Akananuru 24 the man pictures his wife swimming alone through the long cold nights (தமியள் நீந்தி); in Natrinai 341 he pictures her well companioned at play and calls himself the one without company (துணை இலேம் தமியேம்).
links.teaches: With the frame and the closing words the same, the pair shows that the camp poem could place the loneliness on either side, so whether the wife pines or the soldier envies her company was the poet's choice and not something the convention fixed.

links.note: Kural 1222's woman asks the bewildered evening whether its partner is as hard-hearted as hers; Natrinai 343's woman asks whether there is no such evening in the land where her lover went.
links.teaches: Both turn the woman's grief into a question about where evening reaches, but the Natrinai grounds it in a village dusk of cows, offerings and a crow going home to its kin, so the couplet's bare question gains the scene that makes the absent man's freedom from evening seem unnatural.

links.note: Purananuru 158 names Ori as the one who ruled Kolli (கொல்லி ஆண்ட வல்வில் ஓரியும்) among the seven givers now dead; Natrinai 346 measures the wife's fragrant hair by the kulavi of the great cool Kolli of Porayan.
links.teaches: Set beside the elegy that names Ori as Kolli's dead lord, the love poem's passing epithet shows the hill in the Chera Porayan's hands, so the pair records that Kolli changed masters after Ori, which neither poem states.

links.note: Kural 1168's woman says the night that puts every creature to sleep has only her as companion; Natrinai 348's woman lies sleepless while moon, festival town and paired bees all rejoice, and asks whether the world fights her or she the world.
links.teaches: The couplet makes the sleepless woman the night's one companion in a sleeping world, while the Natrinai wakes the whole world in celebration around her, so the same sleeplessness becomes either a bond with the dark or a quarrel with everything else.

links.note: Purananuru 281 has women guard a wounded warrior from ghouls with neem, music, mustard seed and incense; Natrinai 349's man likens himself, ever behind the fisher girl, to the ghoul that hovers by men gravely wounded on the battlefield.
links.teaches: Read with the warding rite, the lover's simile casts him as the very presence a household drives from its wounded with neem and smoke, so his self-portrait as tireless follower carries his knowledge that he is the unwanted one at her door.

links.note: In Natrinai 68 the friend wishes someone would bow and tell the mother that shutting young girls in the house is neither right nor good for it; in 351 she tells the mother herself that the confinement has made the girl paler, that worshipping gods will not help, and that guarding the millet field would restore her.
links.teaches: Together they show the friend's case against the girl's confinement in two stages: a wished-for argument from what is proper, then her own direct plea that adds the evidence of pallor the mother has misread and a cure that quietly returns the girl to her lover's field.

links.note: In Kural 1150 the friend tells the girl, the man overhearing, that the town is raising the very gossip they want; in Natrinai 354 the friend tells the man to his face that his friendship has become gossip as loud as the salt traders' din.
links.teaches: The pair shows the friend aiming the same town gossip toward marriage from two sides: told to the girl in his hearing it is the talk they hoped for, told to the man directly it is a public noise that shames his friendship.

links.note: Kural 580 says that those who want a refinement worth loving will drink poison they see poured; Natrinai 355's friend says the very refined (நனி நாகரிகர்) drink even poison if old friends give it, and asks the man to be kind to the girl by கண் ஓடி.
links.teaches: Valluvar files the poison saying under கண்ணோட்டம; the Natrinai quotes it and then asks for exactly that kindly regard, so the pairing shows the courtesy ideal of the chapter on statecraft working in love poetry as the friend's lever to bind a man to a girl who has no one else.

links.note: Purananuru 67 asks the swan, flying from the ford of Kumari to the northern mountain, to stop at the Chola king's palace with the poet's name; Natrinai 356 likens the man's toiling heart to the swan that grazes the southern sea and carries food to its chicks on the Himalaya.
links.teaches: Both send the swan between the southern sea and the northern mountain, but puram makes it a messenger to a king while akam makes its tireless feeding flight the lover's own heart, so the long-flight swan served as a go-between in one genre and as the self in the other.

links.note: Kural 1207's woman says she does not know forgetting and that even remembering burns; Natrinai 357's woman says the remembered day of play with the man has scarred her heart and will not fade, and on that she says she can bear the delay.
links.teaches: In both, memory cannot be shed, but the couplet makes it a burn and a danger, while the Natrinai makes one remembered day the scar on which the woman rests her claim to endure, so the same unfading memory is wound in one and support in the other.

links.note: Kuruntokai 87's woman meets the belief that the old god of the common destroys the false by saying her lord is not false at all, though her brow pales; Natrinai 358's woman grants that he swore and stays away and goes to make offerings so that the god will not harm him.
links.teaches: Together they show the belief that the oath-god punishes the perjured lover pressing on the woman in two moves, first denial that he is false and then propitiation on the oath-breaker's behalf, so the one he wronged becomes his protector before the god.

links.note: In Kuruntokai 214 the hill girl has been given a great leaf skirt and garland and the whole town is thrown into uproar; in Natrinai 359 the friend, holding the man's gift of leaves, fears the mother if they wear it and hurting him if they return it.
links.teaches: Read together, the leaf skirt shows itself as a public sign of courtship: the Natrinai gives the friend's dilemma before it is worn, and the Kuruntokai gives what follows the wearing, the town's uproar, which is just what the friend feared.

links.note: Kural 1311's woman refuses the philanderer's chest because all women feast on him with their eyes; in Natrinai 360 the friend, or on the colophon's second reading the wife in oodal, refuses him at the door and pictures yesterday's women left like a doll after the festival.
links.teaches: Both refuse the straying husband, but the couplet objects that he is shared, while the Natrinai shows how he uses and discards each courtesan, so the wife's scorn reaches past her own wrong to the rivals he abandons.

source_issues: 345: the colophon thurai reads தௌ¢விடை, a TSCII leftover for தெளிவிடை; copied as printed.
345 line 10, 358 line 4: the TSCII leftover ௌ for ெளி repaired (text flag); 343 line 7, 348 lines 3 and 6: the lost -ஒடு vowel sign restored (text flag); 359 line 4: · read as ஃ (text flag).
343: the colophon thinai is பாலை, but the poem has only mullai things (mullai, cows, the village, evening) and its situation is the woman's waiting; I infer mullai.

358: the colophon's first reading runs together the friend's fear (இவளை இழந்தேன் எனக் கவன்றாள்) and the reassurance (வற்புறுத்தது) without naming who reassures; I take the woman as speaker, as in the second reading. The colophon also prints ஆற்றா ளாயினாள் with a stray space.
354: the colophon begins தோழியால், which reads as a misprint for தோழி.
Natrinai colophons give speaker, addressee and occasion in prose; thurai_akam follows them, and where they name no addressee (341, 345, 348, 359) the code is inferred with a note.
